heading: Purpose
text:
### Purpose [LNOG.1.1]

`logical: false` is a capability setting that bans
`logical`-lifecycle schemas from a DS file, which allows the engine to
omit the Truth Maintenance System (TMS) entirely from the compiled
deployment unit.

The TMS is the subsystem that tracks which token (matching activation)
caused each logical fact to be asserted, and retracts those facts when
the supporting token is retracted.  This cascade can propagate through
chains of logical rules — a retracted input fact may cause a logical
fact to disappear, which may cause a second-order logical fact to
disappear, and so on.  Under `logical: false` this entire subsystem is
absent: no allocation, no cascade bookkeeping, no re-entrancy
constraint.

A program compiled with `logical: false` trades the "automatically retract
derived facts" property in exchange for a strictly simpler retraction
path, a smaller runtime footprint, and elimination of the TMS term from
the T_wcet formula.
